Cold-rich Solvent Pumps –This pump set (2x50%) moves the liquid solvent from the Absorber Sump to the Stripper. The pumps provide the head to pass through the rich side of the LRX and enter the higher-pressure Stripper Vessel. b. Stripper Lean Solvent Pumps –These pumps (2x50%) transfer the hot lean solvent stream from the Stripper Sump to the Absorber to capture CO . The solvent passes through the LRX coolers and Trim 2 Coolers before entry into the Absorber. Two (2) other secondary streams consisting of condensate from the Overhead Condenser and LP CO cooler combine with the lean stream before entering the 2 Absorber. 2.2 Solvent Maintenance Module The Solvent Maintenance Module consists of the components required to charge/fill the capture system with solvent initially, evacuate solvent from the system, and perform washdown maintenance procedures. Maintenance procedures can be performed during system commissioning or decommissioning while the capture system is offline. This section presents all offline or system-level solvent maintenance. Solvent Maintenance Storage Tank collects and stores the solvent from the Absorber and Stripper during a service procedure. The solvent in the Stripper can be evacuated from the sump, through LRX and Trim Attachment-2: Solvent Disposal Investigation 4 DE-FE0031937 / 0003 Coolers, into the Absorber. Valves allow any solvent collected in the Absorber sump to be evacuated via the Solvent Maintenance Pumps. This maintenance procedure typically proceeds with the washdown procedure. The solvent Maintenance Tank heater regulates the temperature of the solvent in the Solvent Maintenance Tank to maintain viscosity within allowable limits and to provide freeze protection. Solvent Washdown Tank is used during service washdowns. The primary objective is to wash down the solvent in the entire Stripper and the Absorber. For this procedure, Wash/Demin water flows to the top of the Stripper for cleaning. The Stripper Lean Pumps evacuate washdown water from the sump, through the LRX and Trim Coolers, into the Absorber. The washdown water continues to flow down through the Absorber into the sump, where valves allow any washdown water collected to be evacuated via the Solvent Maintenance Pumps. Solvent Washdown Tank Heater regulates the temperature of the solvent in the Solvent Washdown Tank to provide freeze protection. Solvent Maintenance Pumps are for maintenance only and serve to move solvent and washdown water from the Absorber, including associated piping, to their respective tank Solvent/Gas Separator separates the gas from the solvent discharge of the Solvent Maintenance Pumps where gas enters the Vessel Vent Header.
